home.tagline: Everything for this role, in one place, with its evidence.
home.why_it_matters: Start here to see what the research changed about the starting account and to pick a route through the material.
do_this: Read the nine corrections in 'How to read this dossier'.
Pick one learning route and tick steps as you go.
Open the key numbers and learn five with their dates and caveats.

read.tagline: Eleven chapters, from first principles to interview answers.
read.why_it_matters: Understanding the business is what lets an answer survive the second follow-up question.
do_this: Read chapter 1 in Beginner view, then again in Technical view.
Stop at each 'Check your understanding' box and answer aloud.
Tap any dotted term for its plain-English definition.

teams.tagline: Geography by client segment, with evidence for every cell.
teams.why_it_matters: You will be asked what the group does and where you see yourself; this shows what is published and what is one person's account.
do_this: Open the two or three teams you could plausibly join and read their briefs.
Note one question to ask for each.
Find a cell marked 'Not publicly established' and practise saying so plainly.

people.tagline: Who is publicly visible, with titles and dates.
people.why_it_matters: Knowing who leads what, and when you last saw it confirmed, prevents an avoidable mistake.
do_this: Learn the group and channel leaders with the date of each source.
Check the 'still in post' field before using any name.
Read the departures: they show how fast this changes.

mandates.tagline: Public wins, losses and partnerships, read carefully.
mandates.why_it_matters: Real cases make answers specific, and the losses make them credible.
do_this: Learn one UK win in detail: client, size, advisers, process.
Learn one loss and what it shows.
For each entry, say what the amount measures.

awareness.tagline: What changed for each client, and what follows.
awareness.why_it_matters: Commercial awareness is a causal chain you can walk through, with dates.
do_this: Pick three cards for your likely teams and rehearse the chain aloud.
For each, say what would change your view.
Prepare one client question per card.

roles.tagline: Who can decide, recommend, or must ask.
roles.why_it_matters: Interviewers test whether you understand what a junior actually does and does not decide.
do_this: Compare institutional sales with relationship management.
Add Summer Analyst as the third column.
Name one task you would own and one you would only support.

lifecycle.tagline: One client, from first research to renewal or exit.
lifecycle.why_it_matters: It links a junior task to a client outcome and a commercial result.
do_this: Step through all twelve stages.
At each, say what the junior produces.
Switch to the wealth-intermediary path and spot three differences.

calculator.tagline: Turn a mandate into revenue, and see what moves it.
calculator.why_it_matters: Being able to do the fee arithmetic aloud shows you understand the economics.
do_this: Reproduce £500m × 20bp = £1m by hand.
Load the tranche, withdrawal and tiered cases and predict each total first.
Change the fee base to committed capital and explain the difference.

why.tagline: Push each reason until it holds or breaks.
why.why_it_matters: 'Why this role?' is asked several ways; a reason that survives five challenges is one you can rely on.
do_this: Answer each level aloud before opening it.
Mark where you repeat yourself.
Fill one row of the personal ledger with real evidence.

practice.tagline: Timed questions, honest scoring, no recording.
practice.why_it_matters: Saying an answer aloud against the clock exposes gaps reading never will.
do_this: Draw ten questions at 90 seconds each.
Score before revealing the reasoning.
Redo your two lowest-scoring questions tomorrow.

glossary.tagline: Every term in plain English first.
glossary.why_it_matters: If you can define a term simply you can use it safely.
do_this: Filter for a term you half-know and read all three fields.
Cover the definition and explain ten acronyms aloud.
Use the quiz's glossary set.

sources.tagline: Every claim, its source and its status.
sources.why_it_matters: Checking the source before you quote something is the habit this project is built on.
do_this: Read the audit of the former intern's claims.
Open the source behind three facts you plan to use.
Read the coverage register to see what was not investigated.

intel.tagline: The sharpest evidence-backed findings, ready to use.
intel.why_it_matters: Specific, dated, sourced points are what separate an informed answer from a generic one. Each card also tells you what a quick read gets wrong.
do_this: Filter to the team you are most likely to meet and read every card.
Say each 'Use it' line aloud in your own words.
Mark a card as learned only when you can state its date and source.

numbers.tagline: The figures worth knowing, with what each one does not show.
numbers.why_it_matters: A correct number with its date and its limit shows precision. A number without its caveat invites a follow-up you cannot answer.
do_this: Open each tile and read the caveat before the value.
Switch on 'Test me' and recall the values from the labels.
Use the charts to explain how assets split by class and channel.

arcade.tagline: Quick drills that tell you what has actually stuck.
arcade.why_it_matters: Recognising a fact on the page is easier than recalling it under pressure. Short, repeated retrieval is how it becomes available in conversation.
do_this: Play one ten-question round a day and note the topics to revisit.
Clear the flashcard deck for the glossary.
Play 'Verified or rumour?' until you can explain why each claim has its status.
